---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Colab (Python and R), your own Linux machine, or AWS"
---

Every lab is a notebook that opens in Google Colab with one click and installs what it needs in
its first cell. You do not need to install anything locally to take the workshop. The local and AWS
routes exist for people who prefer their own machine or must keep data inside their company's cloud.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**What is measured and what is not.** Install times on this page come from runs we recorded (where,
when and on which runtime is stated next to each number). The AWS instructions are written and
scripted but **have not been run by the workshop authors**. The [Readiness](readiness.qmd) page says,
notebook by notebook, what has run where.
:::

## Colab, Python notebooks {#colab-python}

1. Open a lab from the [Notebooks](notebooks.qmd) page or the **Open in Colab** button on a module page.
2. Colab shows *"Warning: This notebook was not authored by Google"*. The notebooks come from this
   workshop's public GitHub repository; read the first cells if you want to see what they do, then
   choose **Run anyway**.
3. Run the first cell (**Install**). It installs the pinned versions of the few libraries Colab does not
   have (for example pymc-marketing and EconML), using the workshop's
   [pinned requirements]({{< var repo.url >}}/blob/main/environment/requirements.txt) as constraints, so
   you get exactly the versions the labs were tested with.
4. If the install cell says **"Runtime > Restart session, then Run all"**, do that. It happens only if a
   different version of PyMC or ArviZ was already imported in the session.

**Measured on Colab** (2026-10-09, Colab runtime `release-colab-external-images_20261007-060045_RC00`,
2 CPUs, Python 3.13.16, recorded in [`spikes/results/s2-colab-python-2026-10-09.json`]({{< var repo.url >}}/blob/main/spikes/results/s2-colab-python-2026-10-09.json)):
installing pymc-marketing 1.2.0, EconML 0.17.0 and nutpie with constraints took **31 s**; importing
pymc-marketing took **17 s**; the first model fit in a fresh session adds roughly **35–45 s** of one-off
compilation. These were measured in a test notebook with the same stack as the labs, not in a lab
itself; each lab's own install time appears below once that lab has a recorded Colab run.

**GPU?** Not needed. These models run on the CPU, and the labs are sized for Colab's free CPU runtime.
A GPU runtime does not make them meaningfully faster and uses up your GPU quota for nothing.

## Colab, R notebooks {#colab-r}

The R labs (Modules 3, 7, 9 and 11, plus the optional Module 0 warm-up) are R notebooks: Colab opens
them in its **R runtime** automatically (Runtime > Change runtime type shows *R*). If a notebook opens
in Python by mistake, switch the runtime type to R and run it again.

The first cell installs the R packages from a dated snapshot of the Posit Public Package Manager
(binary packages, so nothing compiles), adds the GSL system library that CLVTools needs, and installs
GeoLift and augsynth from fixed GitHub commits.

**Measured on Colab** (2026-10-09, same runtime, R 4.6.1, recorded in
[`spikes/results/s3-colab-r-2026-10-09.json`]({{< var repo.url >}}/blob/main/spikes/results/s3-colab-r-2026-10-09.json)):
GSL 9 s; CLVTools 5 s; grf 4 s; CausalImpact with bsts 46 s; GeoLift's dependencies 15 s; augsynth and
GeoLift from GitHub 24 s — about **1 min 45 s** for everything. A lab installs only what it uses.

### Mixing R into a Python notebook (optional)

If you prefer one notebook, the `rpy2` package lets a Python notebook run R cells with the `%%R`
magic. The workshop does not use this route: separate R notebooks are simpler to install and
debug on Colab. If you try it, install the R packages from R first (as the R notebooks do), then
`%pip install rpy2` and `%load_ext rpy2.ipython`.

## Your own Linux machine {#local}

The same image runs locally, in CI and on AWS: R 4.6.1, Python 3.13, JupyterLab and Quarto, defined in
[`environment/Dockerfile`]({{< var repo.url >}}/blob/main/environment/Dockerfile).

**Docker (recommended).**

```bash
git clone {{< var repo.url >}}.git
cd marketing-statistics-workshop
docker build -f environment/Dockerfile -t mktstats-env .
docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8888:8888 \
  -e MKTSTATS_REPO_ROOT=/home/sagemaker-user/work -e PYTHONPATH=/home/sagemaker-user/work/src \
  -v "$PWD":/home/sagemaker-user/work mktstats-env
```

Open the URL with the token that JupyterLab prints. The first build took about 16 minutes on an
Apple Silicon laptop (linux/arm64, 2026-10-09); later builds reuse the cache. On Windows, use WSL 2
(Ubuntu) and follow the same steps.

**VS Code or Codespaces.** The repository has a [devcontainer]({{< var repo.url >}}/tree/main/.devcontainer)
that builds the same image.

**Without Docker (Python only).** With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
uv venv --python 3.13
uv pip install -r environment/requirements.txt
uv pip install -e . --no-deps
.venv/bin/jupyter lab
```

For the R labs without Docker you need R 4.6, the packages in
[`environment/r-packages.txt`]({{< var repo.url >}}/blob/main/environment/r-packages.txt) and IRkernel;
the Docker image is the tested route.

## AWS {#aws}

Two documented routes, both using the same image: **SageMaker Studio** with the workshop image as a
custom image (or a lifecycle configuration for Python only), and **EC2** running JupyterLab from the
image, reached through an SSH tunnel. The step-by-step guide, least-privilege IAM policies, an optional
S3 data bucket and a teardown script are in
[`environment/aws/`]({{< var repo.url >}}/tree/main/environment/aws).

::: {.callout-warning}
**Cost.** Instances, Studio apps and spaces, EBS volumes, ECR images, S3 storage and data transfer are
billed while they exist. Run the teardown script when you finish. See the
[SageMaker AI pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/ai/pricing/) and
[EC2 On-Demand pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/) pages; this site does not quote prices.
The AWS route **has not been run by the workshop authors**.
:::

## Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}

| Symptom | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Runtime > Restart session, then Run all" | Do exactly that: an older PyMC or ArviZ was imported before the install cell ran. |
| An R notebook opens with Python | Runtime > Change runtime type > R, then run the first cell again. |
| A download fails (dataset or package) | Run the cell again; the loaders retry and fall back to a mirror where the licence allows. Tell the instructor if it keeps failing. |
| A model fit is much slower than the lab says | Check you are not on a TPU/GPU runtime by mistake, and that `QUICK` is as the lab says. First fits in a session include compilation. |
| A checkpoint fails on the reference solution | That is a problem with the lab or the runtime, not your code: tell the instructor. |
| "TODO n is not written yet" | Write the exercise, run its cell, then rerun the checkpoint; or continue with `workshop.use_reference(n)`. |
